params.owner_: Initial contract owner (Ownable). Typically the deployer or a timelock.

returns.updatedAt: block.timestamp at which the price was last confirmed valid.                   VaultEngine additionally validates this against MAX_ORACLE_STALENESS.

returns.price: Most recent USD price (18 decimals). 0 if never set.
returns.updatedAt: Timestamp of the most recent price update. 0 if never set.

returns._0: True if a non-zero aggregator is registered; false otherwise.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

params.aggregator: Chainlink AggregatorV3Interface address. Must be non-zero.
params.token: Collateral token address. Must be non-zero.
Collateral token address whose feed should be removed.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

params.usdPrice18: USD price with 18 decimal places (e.g. $3 247.50 = 3247.5e18). Must be > 0.

params.prices: Corresponding USD prices with 18 decimals. Each must be > 0.
params.tokens: Array of collateral token addresses. Must be the same length as `prices`.

params.newMaxStaleness: New staleness threshold in seconds. Must be ≥ 300.

params.newUpdater: Address to grant the updater role. May be address(0) to clear it.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

WAD().notice: 1 WAD = 1e18. All prices returned by this contract are WAD-scaled.

constructor.notice: Deploy the oracle with no registered feeds and no updater set.         Call setUpdater() after deployment to authorise the keeper bot address.         Seed fallback prices via setFallbackPrices() and register Chainlink feeds         via registerFeed() as needed.

feeds(address).notice: Chainlink AggregatorV3 feed registered for each collateral token.         address(0) means no feed is registered; fallback price is used.

getPrice(address).notice: Returns the current USD price for `token` with staleness enforcement.         Priority: Chainlink feed (if registered and fresh) → admin fallback (if ≤ 24h old).         Reverts if no valid, non-stale price is available.         This is the only function that should be called from protocol logic         (mintUsdax, liquidate, health-factor checks).

getPriceUnsafe(address).notice: Returns the most recently known price for `token` WITHOUT staleness checks.         Intended for off-chain UI display, monitoring dashboards, and test helpers.         MUST NOT be called from liquidation, mint, or any other protocol safety logic.         Returns (0, 0) if no price has ever been set for the token.

hasFeed(address).notice: Returns whether a Chainlink feed is currently registered for a token.         A `true` result does not guarantee the feed is fresh or returning valid data.

maxStaleness().notice: Maximum age (seconds) for a Chainlink round answer before it is treated         as stale and the fallback price is used instead. Default: 1 hour.         Can be raised for less-liquid assets with slower feed update cadences.

registerFeed(address,address).notice: Register a Chainlink AggregatorV3 feed for a collateral token.         After registration, getPrice() will prefer the Chainlink feed over the fallback.         On Robinhood Chain mainnet (4663) call this after deployment with the addresses         documented in the contract-level NatSpec.         Only callable by the contract owner.

removeFeed(address).notice: Remove the Chainlink feed for a token.         After removal, getPrice() falls back to the admin-set price.         Only callable by the contract owner.

setFallbackPrice(address,uint256).notice: Set a single admin fallback price.         The fallback is used when no Chainlink feed is registered or the feed is stale.         On testnet this is the primary (only) price source; the keeper refreshes it         every 30 minutes from a CoinGecko feed to keep it within the 24-hour validity window.         Callable by the contract owner OR the designated updater (keeper bot).

setFallbackPrices(address[],uint256[]).notice: Batch-set admin fallback prices for multiple tokens in one transaction.         Useful for the keeper's periodic refresh to minimise gas and round-trip latency.         Callable by the contract owner OR the designated updater (keeper bot).

setMaxStaleness(uint256).notice: Update the maximum Chainlink answer age before it is treated as stale.         A shorter window gives stronger freshness guarantees but may cause reverts         during Chainlink downtime. A longer window is appropriate for less-liquid assets.         Minimum allowed value is 300 seconds (5 minutes) to prevent misconfiguration.         Only callable by the contract owner.

setUpdater(address).notice: Assign or replace the updater address — the account authorised to push         fallback prices without full owner privileges.         Set to the keeper bot EOA on testnet; on mainnet use a dedicated hot wallet         or a separate Gnosis Safe with a lower signing threshold.         Set to address(0) to revoke the role (only owner may push prices).         Only callable by the contract owner (or timelock on production).

updater().notice: Address authorised to push fallback prices (setFallbackPrice / setFallbackPrices).         Separate from the contract owner so the keeper bot can update prices frequently         without having governance-level admin rights. address(0) = only owner may push prices.         Set via setUpdater(). On mainnet, set this to a dedicated keeper EOA or multisig;         on testnet, the deployer serves as both owner and updater.
